chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Wallād and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān together, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

It is appropriate for the relatives of your deceased to inform the deceased’s brothers of his death, so that they may attend his جنازة, perform salat over him, and seek forgiveness for him. Thus reward is obtained for them, forgiveness is recorded for the deceased, and he himself gains reward through what has been obtained for him of seeking forgiveness.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَيِّتِ: the relatives or responsible guardians of the deceased
key_terms.إِخْوَانَ الْمَيِّتِ: the fellow believers or brethren of the deceased
key_terms.الِاسْتِغْفَارِ: seeking divine forgiveness on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.يُصَلُّونَ عَلَيْهِ: they perform the funeral salat over him

ai.seo_question: Why should the family of a deceased person inform others about the death in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the family of the deceased should notify his fellow believers of his death so they can attend the funeral, perform salat over him, and seek forgiveness for him. It highlights the communal benefit of funeral participation: the living receive reward, and the deceased benefits from their istighfar and the reward connected to it.
